text:
Predicates:
PerformsInSchoolTalentShow(x) ::: x performs in school talent shows often.
AttendsSchoolEvents(x) ::: x attends and is very engaged with school events.
ActiveMember(x) ::: x is an active member of the community.
InactiveMember(x) ::: x is inactive and disinterested in the community.
ChaperonesHighSchoolDance(x) ::: x chaperones high school dances.
Student(x) ::: x is a student who attends the school.
WishesToFurtherAcademic(x) ::: x wishes to further academic careers and educational opportunities.
YoungChildOrTeenager(x) ::: x is a young child or teenager.

Premises:
∀x (PerformsInSchoolTalentShow(x) → AttendsSchoolEvents(x)) ::: If people perform in school talent shows often, then they attend and are very engaged with school events.
∀x (PerformsInSchoolTalentShow(x) ∨ (InactiveMember(x) ∧ DisinterestedMember(x))) ::: People either perform in school talent shows often or are inactive and disinterested members of their community.
∀x (ChaperonesHighSchoolDance(x) → ¬Student(x)) ::: If people chaperone high school dances, then they are not students who attend the school.
∀x (InactiveMember(x) ∧ DisinterestedMember(x) → ChaperonesHighSchoolDance(x)) ::: All inactive and disinterested members chaperone high school dances.
∀x (YoungChildOrTeenager(x) ∧ WishesToFurtherAcademic(x) → Student(x)) ::: All young children and teenagers who wish to further their academic careers are students who attend the school.
BonnieAttendsAndEngaged ∧ BonnieStudent ∨ ¬(BonnieAttendsAndEngaged) ∧ ¬(BonnieStudent) ::: Bonnie either both attends and is very engaged with school events and is a student, or neither.

Conclusion:
(YoungChildOrTeenager(Bonnie) ∧ WishesToFurtherAcademic(Bonnie) ∧ ChaperonesHighSchoolDance(Bonnie)) ∨ (¬YoungChildOrTeenager(Bonnie) ∧ ¬WishesToFurtherAcademic(Bonnie)) → (Student(Bonnie) ∨ InactiveMember(Bonnie))
